Back: of(value) requires a non-null value and throws NullPointerException on null. ofNullable(value) returns Optional.empty() when the value is null, e.g. `Optional.ofNullable(payments.get(id))` in a Map-based repository. empty() states absence explicitly.

map() is for a mapper that returns a plain value: `payment.map(Payment::getAmount)` gives Optional<BigDecimal>. flatMap() is for a mapper that already returns an Optional; using map() there gives Optional<Optional<String>>. If the Optional is empty, neither mapper runs.

orElse(value) evaluates its argument before the call, even when the Optional has a value, so `orElse(createFallbackPayment())` always runs the method. orElseGet(Supplier) only runs the supplier when the Optional is empty. Use orElseGet for costly fallbacks (DB call, network, object creation).

Front: Why does the repository return Optional<Payment> while the service calls orElseThrow()?
Back: The repository only reports found or not found, without null in its contract. The service decides what absence means for the use case: for GET /payments/{id} it throws PaymentNotFoundException(id); another use case could fall back to a default instead.

Front: What does GET /payments/999 return when the service throws PaymentNotFoundException and nothing handles it?
Back: 500 Internal Server Error: Spring treats any unhandled exception as a server error. To return 404 Not Found you map the exception, e.g. with @ControllerAdvice + @ExceptionHandler (Day 22) or @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND) on the exception class.
